LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why should people write neatly? 2. How can we spell words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner’s self-discipline is enhanced as they are motivated practise correct letter formation and writing words related to

target sounds.

Values:
Responsibility: is developed as learners take different roles while engaging in group and pair activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-esteem is promoted as learner acquires enhanced level of self-esteem as they write legibly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili Language Activities as learners relate formation of the target letters correctly in terms of shape and size for effective

communication.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
